hints: Find the acceleration from the given kinematics: $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $s = 4.5\text{ m}$ and $t = 5\text{ s}$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $6\cos\theta - F = ma$, where $\cos\theta = \frac{24}{25}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the acceleration of the block during the first $5\text{ s}$ from rest:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
$$4.5 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}a(5^2) = 12.5a \implies a = \frac{4.5}{12.5} = 0.36\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally with pulling force component $6\cos\theta = 6\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) = 5.76\text{ N}$:
$$6\cos\theta - F = ma$$
$$5.76 - F = 3(0.36) = 1.08$$

Solve for the frictional force $F$:
$$F = 5.76 - 1.08 = 4.68\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the constant acceleration from rest using the displacement formula:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
Substitute $u = 0$, $s = 4.5\text{ m}$, and $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$4.5 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}a(5^2)$$
$$4.5 = 12.5a$$
Divide by $12.5$:
$$a = \frac{4.5}{12.5} = \frac{9}{25} = 0.36\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law in the horizontal direction:
$$\Sigma F_x = ma \implies 6\cos\theta - F = ma$$
Substitute $\cos\theta = \frac{24}{25} = 0.96$, $m = 3\text{ kg}$, and $a = 0.36\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$6 \times 0.96 - F = 3 \times 0.36$$
$$5.76 - F = 1.08$$
Subtract $1.08$ from $5.76$:
$$F = 5.76 - 1.08 = 4.68\text{ N}$$

walkthrough:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium to find the normal reaction $R$:
$$R + 6\sin\theta = mg$$
$$R = 3(10) - 6(0.28) = 30 - 1.68 = 28.32\text{ N}$$

Apply the friction law $F = \mu R$ to find the coefficient of friction $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{4.68}{28.32} = \frac{39}{236} \approx 0.165254 \approx 0.165$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the upward component of the $6\text{ N}$ pulling force:
From $\cos\theta = \frac{24}{25}$, the angle belongs to a 7-24-25 right triangle, so:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{7}{25} = 0.28$$
The vertical force component is $6\sin\theta = 6 \times 0.28 = 1.68\text{ N}$.

State the vertical equilibrium condition for the block:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies R + 6\sin\theta - mg = 0$$
$$R = mg - 6\sin\theta = 3 \times 10 - 1.68 = 30 - 1.68 = 28.32\text{ N}$$

Use the limiting friction formula $F = \mu R$:
$$4.68 = \mu \times 28.32$$
Divide by $28.32$:
$$\mu = \frac{4.68}{28.32} = \frac{468}{2832} = \frac{39}{236} \approx 0.165254$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures confirms $\mu = 0.165$.

hints: Find the speed of the block at $t = 5\text{ s}$: $v = at = 0.36(5) = 1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
When the $6\text{ N}$ force is removed, the normal reaction becomes $R = mg = 30\text{ N}$.
Calculate the new deceleration under friction alone: $a = -\mu g = -0.165(10) = -1.65\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Find the stopping time $t_2 = \frac{1.8}{1.65}$ and add $5\text{ s}$ to obtain the total time.
walkthrough:
Find the speed reached by the block after $5\text{ s}$:
$$v = u + at = 0 + 0.36(5) = 1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

When the pulling force is removed, the normal reaction is simply the weight of the block:
$$R_{\text{new}} = mg = 3(10) = 30\text{ N}$$
The frictional deceleration is:
$$a_2 = -\frac{\mu R_{\text{new}}}{m} = -\mu g = -0.165(10) = -1.65\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Find the time $t_2$ taken to decelerate from $1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to rest:
$$0 = 1.8 + (-1.65)t_2 \implies 1.65t_2 = 1.8 \implies t_2 = \frac{1.8}{1.65} \approx 1.091\text{ s}$$

Calculate the total time of motion:
$$t_{\text{total}} = 5 + 1.091 = 6.091\text{ s} \approx 6.09\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the velocity of the block at the moment the $6\text{ N}$ force is removed ($t = 5\text{ s}$):
$$v = u + a_1 t_1 = 0 + 0.36 \times 5 = 1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Determine the new normal reaction and frictional force during the deceleration phase:
Without the pulling force, there is no vertical component lifting the block:
$$R = mg = 3 \times 10 = 30\text{ N}$$
The new frictional force is:
$$F = \mu R = 0.165254 \times 30 \approx 4.9576\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law for the deceleration phase:
$$-F = ma_2 \implies -4.9576 = 3a_2 \implies a_2 = -1.6525\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the additional time $t_2$ to come to rest:
$$v_{\text{final}} = v + a_2 t_2$$
$$0 = 1.8 - 1.6525 t_2$$
$$1.6525 t_2 = 1.8 \implies t_2 = \frac{1.8}{1.6525} \approx 1.089\text{ s}$$

Find the total duration of motion from the beginning:
$$t_{\text{total}} = t_1 + t_2 = 5 + 1.089 = 6.089\text{ s}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $t_{\text{total}} = 6.09\text{ s}$.
